alarm_codes.description: Travel limit exceeded. Commanded position beyond soft limit for any axis.

Check A/C angles with TCP compensation
Reduce part size or reposition on table

alarm_codes.description: Spindle speed command error. S-value exceeds 15000 RPM or is zero during cut.
corrective_actions: Reduce S to within 50-15000
Check tool-specific RPM limits
Verify S word present before cuts

alarm_codes.description: RTCP (TCP) position error. Tool center point position deviation exceeded tolerance during 5-axis motion. Calculated linear axis compensation exceeds axis travel or acceleration limits.
probable_causes: Part mounted too far from A/C axis center of rotation
Tool length offset error creating excessive TCP lever arm
Rapid A/C change rate requiring impossible linear axis velocity
Work offset origin too far from trunnion center
corrective_actions: Verify part is centered on trunnion table (within 100mm of C-axis center)
Check tool length offset measurement accuracy
Reduce 5-axis feed rate to allow linear axes to keep up
Reposition WCS origin closer to A/C center of rotation

alarm_codes.description: TCP tool vector error. G43.5 tool vector (I/J/K) is not a unit vector or is undefined.
probable_causes: I/J/K values do not form a unit vector (sqrt(I^2+J^2+K^2) != 1)
corrective_actions: Normalize tool vectors to unit length
Fix post processor vector output
Add I/J/K to G43.5 blocks

alarm_codes.description: A-axis servo error excessive. Trunnion tilt axis following error exceeded threshold.
probable_causes: Table overloaded beyond A-axis tilt capacity at current angle
A-axis clamp engaged during motion command
Workpiece shifted on table causing imbalance
corrective_actions: Check table load vs A-angle derating chart
Verify M69 (clamp OFF) before A-axis motion
Listen for abnormal trunnion bearing noise
Verify workpiece is securely clamped and balanced

alarm_codes.description: C-axis servo error excessive. Table rotation axis following error exceeded threshold.
probable_causes: Off-center workpiece creating high inertia moment
corrective_actions: Verify M69 clamp OFF before C-axis rotation
Check for chip accumulation around table base
Reduce C-axis rotation speed for heavy parts
Verify workpiece is centered on table

alarm_codes.description: A-axis overtravel. Trunnion tilt exceeded -120 or +30 degree limits.
probable_causes: Post processor not clamping A output
TCP compensation generating A values beyond range
corrective_actions: Verify A-axis program values within -120 to +30
Fix post processor A-axis limits
Adjust part orientation to avoid extreme A angles

alarm_codes.description: Thermo-Friendly Concept compensation out of range. Thermal growth has exceeded the correction model limits.

Temperature sensor fault returning incorrect readings

Verify spindle cooler is maintaining set temperature
Check all thermal compensation sensors on diagnostic page
If shop temp unstable, allow machine to stabilize for 2 hours before precision work

alarm_codes.description: Thermal compensation sensor failure. One or more temperature sensors for Thermo-Friendly Concept not responding.
corrective_actions: Check sensor connections on diagnostic screen — identify failed sensor number
Inspect sensor wiring at the identified location
Replace failed sensor

programming_tips.code_example:
G05 P2 (Super NURBS ON)
G43.4 H1 (TCP ON)
G06.2 K3 X0. Y0. Z0. R1. X10. Y5. Z-0.5 R1.2 X20. Y10. Z-1. R1. X30. Y5. Z-0.5 R1.
G01 A-30. C45. F8000 (Simultaneous 5-axis with NURBS)
G05 P0 (NURBS OFF)
G49 (TCP OFF)
programming_tips.description: The P500A's Super NURBS (G05 P2 + G06.2) produces smoother surfaces than linearized toolpaths because the controller follows mathematical curves directly instead of interpolating between line segments. Combined with TCP (G43.4), this enables 5-axis surface finishing that eliminates the faceted appearance common with linearized CAM output. The CAM system must output NURBS format, which Mastercam, hyperMILL, and NX support via dedicated OSP post processors.
gotchas: Not all CAM systems support NURBS output for OSP — verify post processor capability
NURBS mode increases processing time per block — reduce number of control points where curvature is gentle
Super NURBS combined with 5-axis TCP is the P500A's most compute-intensive mode — 2000-block look-ahead helps
Weight values R < 1 pull curve away from control point, R > 1 pulls toward — use for blending transitions

programming_tips.topic: 5-Axis TCP Setup — A/C Trunnion Table Configuration
programming_tips.code_example:
G43.4 H1 (TCP ON — pivot point compensation active)
G00 A0. C0. (Table horizontal, no rotation)
G01 X50. Y0. Z-5. A-45. C30. F800
(Linear axes automatically compensate as A/C rotate)
...
G49 (TCP OFF)
G00 A0. C0. (Return table to home)
programming_tips.description: TCP (G43.4) is the foundation of all 5-axis work on the MU-5000V. It compensates for the distance between the tool tip and the A/C axis center of rotation. Without TCP, tilting the table (A-axis) would move the part relative to the tool. The MU-5000V stores the trunnion pivot point location in machine parameters — this must be calibrated quarterly (see MAINT-011). The tool length offset (H value) must be measured accurately because TCP amplifies any error by the lever arm distance.
gotchas: Tool length offset error is AMPLIFIED by TCP — 0.1mm error at tool tip becomes 0.5mm+ error at 5-axis angles
Work offset origin should be as close to the A/C center of rotation as possible to minimize linear axis travel during tilts
TCP compensation can push linear axes to travel limits at extreme A angles — verify with dry run
G49 must be called before G28 home return — homing with TCP active causes incorrect axis positions

programming_tips.topic: Thermo-Friendly Concept Utilization for Precision Work
programming_tips.code_example:
(Thermo-Friendly is always active — no G-code needed)
(Force recalibration before critical features:)
M350 (Trigger thermal compensation recalibration)
G04 P5000 (Dwell 5 sec for measurement)
(Now machine critical feature with fresh thermal data)
G01 Z-10.000 F200 (Precision bore depth)
programming_tips.description: The MU-5000V's Thermo-Friendly Concept continuously monitors 8+ temperature sensors on the spindle, column, bed, and trunnion. It applies real-time compensation to axis positions based on a thermal model. This system reduces warmup time and maintains accuracy during long machining cycles even as ambient temperature changes. However, it does NOT replace spindle warmup — the bearings still need lubrication distribution from warmup rotation. M350 forces a recalibration measurement before critical features.
gotchas: Thermo-Friendly reduces but does NOT eliminate thermal error — expect +/-3um in stable conditions
Rapid ambient temperature changes (>5 deg C/hour) can exceed compensation range (TH0001 alarm)
Opening the machine door during cutting allows thermal shock — keep door closed during precision work
M350 recalibration takes 3-5 seconds — include G04 dwell after M350 before critical cuts

programming_tips.code_example:
(Register tool models in P500A anti-crash setup screen)
(1. Define holder geometry for each tool pocket)
(2. Define fixture model — import from CAD or manual entry)
(3. Enable: Parameter > Safety > Anti-Crash = ON)

(In program:)
M310 (Checkpoint at ATC and A/C repositioning)
G43.4 H1
G00 A-45. C90. (Anti-crash verifies this move is safe)
G01 X50. Y0. Z-10. F1000
programming_tips.description: The MU-5000V anti-crash system models the spindle, tool holders, fixtures, and workpiece in 3D and checks every commanded motion before execution. On the P500A, this system is significantly faster than on P300 (10ms vs 50ms overhead per block). Tool holder models, fixture models, and the workpiece blank must be registered accurately. M310 forces a full recalculation at critical points. The system checks both cutting and rapid moves.
gotchas: Anti-crash is ONLY as accurate as the registered models — measure all tool holders carefully
Fixture models must be updated when fixtures change — stale model = false safety
Anti-crash adds 10ms per block overhead on P500A — negligible for most operations
M311/M312 temporarily disables anti-crash for probing — ALWAYS re-enable with M312 immediately after probe cycle

programming_tips.topic: OSP Macro Variable System — #VC/#VE Extended Variables on P500A
programming_tips.code_example:
VC1 = 50.0 (Common variable — tool diameter)
VC2 = 0.5 (Stepover ratio)
VC10 = VC1 * VC2 (Calculated stepover = 25mm)

VE100 = 1 (P500A extended variable — cycle count)
VE101 = VSPLD (Store spindle load reading)

VUSR1 = VE100 (Copy to persistent storage — survives power off)

IF [VE101 GT 80] GOTO 9000
(Adaptive feed based on spindle load)
programming_tips.description: The P500A expands the macro variable system: VC1-999 (common), VE1-500 (extended, P500A only), VB1-100 (boolean), and VUSR1-500 (persistent, tripled from P300's 200). System variables like VSPLD (spindle load), VACTX/VACTZ (actual position), and VTLF[n] (tool life) provide real-time machine data. The 8-level nesting depth (vs 4 on P300) enables more complex adaptive programs.
gotchas: VE variables are P500A only — programs using VE will not run on P300 machines
VUSR variables persist across power cycles — use for tool life counters and production metrics
8-level nesting allows complex logic but deeper nesting adds execution time
VSPLD and VACTX update every servo cycle but macro reads have 50-100ms latency

programming_tips.topic: Table Load vs Tilt Angle Derating for A-Axis
programming_tips.code_example:
(Load derating chart — DO NOT exceed these limits:)
(A = 0 degrees (horizontal): 400 kg max)
(A = -30 degrees: 350 kg max)
(A = -60 degrees: 280 kg max)
(A = -90 degrees (vertical): 200 kg max)
(A = -120 degrees: 150 kg max)

(Check in macro before tilt:)
IF [VC50 GT 200] THEN
  IF [VACTA LT -60] GOTO 9500
END
N9500 M01 (OVERWEIGHT FOR THIS TILT ANGLE)
programming_tips.description: The MU-5000V trunnion table supports 400kg when horizontal (A=0) but this capacity decreases as the table tilts. At A=-90 (vertical), capacity drops to 200kg. At A=-120 (maximum tilt for undercut access), capacity is only 150kg. Exceeding these limits causes A-axis servo errors, potential trunnion bearing damage, and crash risk. Program a macro check that compares known workpiece weight against A-angle to prevent overload.
gotchas: Workpiece weight includes the fixture — measure TOTAL weight on table
Dynamic cutting forces add to the static load — derate by 20% for heavy roughing
Off-center loading is worse than centered — keep workpiece within 100mm of table center
A-axis servo alarm (AC0001) during tilt is almost always a weight problem

programming_tips.topic: 3+2 Machining Setup with G68.2 Tilted Working Plane
programming_tips.code_example:
G28 X0. Y0. Z0. (Home first)
G68.2 X0. Y0. Z0. I0. J-45. K0. (Tilt WCS 45 deg around Y)
M68 (Clamp A/C axes)
G43.4 H1 (TCP ON)
G54 (Activate WCS)
G00 X0. Y0.
G43 Z50. H1
G01 Z-5. F500 (Cutting in tilted plane)
...
G49 (TCP OFF)
G69 (Cancel tilted plane)
M69 (Unclamp A/C)
G00 A0. C0. (Return to home)
programming_tips.description: G68.2 defines a tilted working plane using Euler angles (I=rotation about X, J=rotation about Y, K=rotation about Z). The controller calculates the required A/C axis positions and transforms all XYZ moves into the tilted coordinate system. For 3+2 work, the A/C axes are positioned ONCE then clamped (M68) — no simultaneous A/C motion during cutting. This is more rigid than 5-axis simultaneous and preferred for roughing and drilling at angles.
gotchas: G43.4 TCP is REQUIRED with G68.2 — without it, positions are wrong in the tilted plane
Euler angle convention on Okuma is Z-Y-X (applied as Z rotation first, then Y, then X)
Cancel G68.2 with G69 before any axis homing or ATC operations
M68 (clamp) AFTER the A/C axes reach position — clamping before move causes servo alarm

programming_tips.topic: P500A Smooth Machining Mode (G05.4) for Surface Quality
programming_tips.code_example:
G187 E3 (Accuracy priority)
G05.4 Q1 (P500A Smooth Machining ON)
G43.4 H1 (TCP ON)
G01 X... Y... Z... A... C... F10000
(5-axis simultaneous finishing with smoothing)
G05.4 Q0 (Smooth Machining OFF)
G49
programming_tips.description: G05.4 is exclusive to the OSP-P500A and represents the latest generation of Okuma's path control technology. It combines AI-based look-ahead with servo prediction algorithms to minimize acceleration-induced surface marks that appear as witness lines on machined surfaces. Use G05.4 with G187 E3 for the highest surface quality. This mode is especially effective during 5-axis simultaneous finishing where A/C axis motion creates variable effective feed rates.
gotchas: G05.4 is P500A ONLY — will alarm on P300 controllers
Reduces effective feed rate by 20-40% to eliminate surface marks — account for in cycle time
Most effective when combined with G187 E3 — using with E1 (rough) provides minimal benefit
2000-block look-ahead on P500A makes G05.4 significantly smoother than G05.1 on P300

programming_tips.topic: Probing for 5-Axis Part Alignment on Trunnion Table
programming_tips.code_example:
(Step 1: Probe datum features at A=0 C=0)
G31 Z-50. F300 (Probe top face)
VC10 = VACTZ (Store Z touch position)

(Step 2: Probe at rotated C position)
G00 C90.
G31 X-25. F200 (Probe side face)
VC11 = VACTX

(Step 3: Calculate and set WCS)
G10 L2 P1 X[VC11] Z[VC10]

(Step 4: G10.9 for tilted parts)
G10.9 X[p1x] Y[p1y] Z[p1z] I[p2x] J[p2y] K[p2z] U[p3x] V[p3y] W[p3z]
programming_tips.description: 5-axis part alignment on the MU-5000V combines touch probing (G31) with coordinate transforms (G10.9) and rotary positioning. For parts fixtured on the trunnion, probe at multiple C-angles to establish the part coordinate system. G10.9 handles the case where the part is not perfectly level on the table by computing a tilted WCS from three probed points. The P500A's G31.3 allows probing with simultaneous A/C motion for complex shapes.
gotchas: Probe stylus deflection compensation must match actual probe — calibrate on reference sphere first
G10.9 three-point alignment requires non-collinear points — use points at least 50mm apart
Probing with A/C rotation (G31.3) is slower than fixed-angle probing — use only when necessary
Store all probed values in macro variables BEFORE calculating offsets — re-probing after G10.9 could give different results

programming_tips.topic: High-Speed Machining Configuration for Aluminum Aerospace Parts
programming_tips.code_example:
G187 E1 (Rough: fast corners, lower accuracy)
G05 P10000 (HSM path smoothing ON)
G43.4 H1
S15000 M03 (Max RPM for aluminum)
G01 X... Y... Z... F12000 (HSM roughing)
...
G187 E3 (Finish: accurate corners)
G05.4 Q1 (P500A Smooth Machining)
S15000
G01 ... F8000 (Finish contouring)
programming_tips.description: For aluminum aerospace parts, the MU-5000V can run at full 15000 RPM with 37kW power. Use G187 E1 for roughing (allows corner rounding for higher feed rates) and G187 E3 for finishing (maintains programmed path accuracy). HSM mode (G05 P10000) smooths toolpath corners to prevent deceleration. The P500A's 2000-block look-ahead is critical for HSM — it prevents feed starving that causes surface marks. Through-spindle coolant (M50) is essential for deep pocket work in aluminum.
gotchas: At 15000 RPM, HSK-A63 drawbar force is reduced — maximum tool holder weight is 6kg at full speed
G187 E1 can round corners by up to 0.5mm — not suitable for finish passes
Feed starving shows as shiny bands on aluminum — increase look-ahead buffer to maximum in P500A settings
Through-spindle coolant (M50) at 70 bar can blow chips back into the cut in shallow pockets — use flood (M08) for finishing
